title: Kafka 이벤트에 데이터를 어디까지 실어야 할까 - Thin vs Fat
partialText:
들어가며

Kafka를 배우고 실행에 옮기다 여기저기서 들은 말이 있습니다.

  • A. 이벤트는 간단해야 한다. ID만 실어서 보내고 필요한 데이터는 받는 쪽이 조회해라.
  • B. 이벤트에 필요한 정보 전부를 실어서 보내야 한다. 받는 쪽이 아무것도 안 물어보고 일을 끝낼 수 있어야 한다.

과연 무엇이 정답일까? 계속해서 고민했습니다. 역시나 이 문제도 정답이 존재하지 않습니다.

위 두 패턴은 이름이 존재합니다. 각각 Thin Event, Fat Event입니다. Thin Event는 결합을 Fat Event는 장애 전파를 두려워 합니다. 이 둘이 막고자하는 것이 다른 것입니다.

문제의 발견

trusta-market 프로젝트를 진행하며 제가 맡은 도메인은 검수와 배송이었습니다. 배송 흐름은 다음과 같습니다.

주문 결제 완료
   ↓ OrderPaidEvent (Kafka)
배송 서비스: 배송 테이블에 적재
   ↓ AM/PM 스케줄러 (오전 9시 / 오후 2시) 배치
   ↓ CarrierDeliveryRequestedKafkaEvent (Kafka)
mock-carrier-service (CJ·한진 등 외부 택배사 시뮬레이션. 현재는 mock)
   ↓ 운송 완료 이벤트 (Kafka)
배송 서비스: 배송 완료 처리

여기서 배송 -> carrier로 나가던 메시지가 이랬습니다.

public record CarrierDeliveryRequestedKafkaEvent(
        UUID deliveryId,
        String deliveryType,
        UUID productId,
        UUID senderId,
        UUID receiverId    // <- 받는 사람을 ID로만 전달
) {
}

전부 ID를 필드로 가진 Thin Event였습니다. 그런데 택배사가 배송을 하려면 주소가 필요합니다. 이 메시지엔 주소가 없고, receiverId만 존재했습니다. 계속 테스트를 진행했음에도 불구하고, 문제로 보이지 않았던 이유는 바로 mock-carrier-service가 주소를 쓰지 않고 그냥 "운송 완료"를 찍어줬기 때문입니다. mock이 문제를 가린 것이었습니다. 하지만 이걸 mock이 아닌 CJ나 한진으로 변경하는 순간, 이 메시지로는 배송이 불가능해집니다. MVP 구현에 급급한 나머지, 잘못된 설계를 진행했던 것이었습니다. "어차피 가짜니까 대충하지"가 아니라 "통제 불가능한 외부 시스템을 시뮬레이션해야지"라는 마음가짐으로 설계했어야 했습니다. 오로지 저의 불찰이었습니다.

판단 기준

다음 3개의 질문으로 Thin 필드로 구성할지, Fat 필드로 구성할지 정할 수 있습니다.

질문 1. 받는 쪽이 이 데이터 없이 자기 일을 끝낼 수 있나?

  • 못 끝낸다면 무조건 Fat입니다.
  • 끝낼 수 있다면 질문 2로 갑니다.

질문 2. 받는 쪽이 되물어 볼 수 있는 상대인가?

  • 외부 경계(위 경우와 마찬가지인 택배사 등) -> 되물을 수 없다. -? Fat
  • 내부 서비스 -> 되물을 수 있다 -> 질문 3으로 갑니다.

질문 3. 그 데이터는 그 시점의 사실이어야 하나, 항상 최신이어야 하나?

  • 그 시점의 사실(주문 시점의 가격, 주소 등) -> Fat
  • 항상 최신이어야 함 -> Thin(조회)

한 줄로 요약하자면, 못 끝내면 싣고, 못 되물으면 싣고, 시점 사실이면 싣습니다.

적용

배송 주소에 적용해보면 전부 Fat을 가리킵니다.

  1. 주소가 없으면 배송 불가 -> Fat
  2. 최종 소비자가 외부라 되물을 수 없음 -> Fat
  3. 주문 시점의 배송지여야 함 -> Fat

여기서 3번이 중요합니다. 사용자가 오전 10시에 회사로 도착하도록 주문했는데, 배송 배치는 2시에 돕니다. 그 사이 사용자가 회원 정보 기본 배송지를 집으로 바꿨을 때, 배송 시점에 회원 서비스를 조회(Thin)하면 바뀐 집 주소로 잘못 배송됩니다. 하지만 주문 시점 주소를 스냅샷으로 박제(Fat)하면 의도한 회사로 배송됩니다. 배송지는 회원의 현재 상태가 아닌 주문이라는 사건의 일부입니다. 그래서 주문 시점에 박제되어 이벤트를 타고 흘러야 합니다.

만약 ID만 남겨뒀다면?

buyerId만 두고 배송 배치 때 회원 서비스를 조회하는 구조였다면 다음과 같은 로직이 실행될 것입니다.

public void dispatchBatch() {
    List<Delivery> pending = deliveryRepository.findPending(); // 1000건
    for (Delivery d : pending) {
        BuyerInfo buyer = memberClient.getBuyer(d.getBuyerId()); // 건당 Feign 호출
        carrierProducer.send(toCarrierRequest(d, buyer.address()));
    }
}

보기만 해도 아찔한 문제가 발생합니다.

  1. N번 호출: 배송 1000건이면 회원 서비스를 1000번 호출합니다. 배치가 몰리는 시간대에 부하 스파이크가 발생합니다.
  2. 장애 전파: 오전 9시, 오후 2시에 회원 서비스가 죽어 있으면, 결제까지 끝난 배송 전체가 진행되지 않습니다.
  3. 정합성 버그: 위에서 언급한 바뀐 주소 문제가 발생합니다.

결과

결과적으로 한 이벤트 안에 Thin과 Fat이 공존합니다. 식별자(buyerId)는 Thin, 시점 사실(주소)은 Fat. 한 이벤트 안에서 섞이는 게 정상이고, 그게 가장 좋은 것이라 생각합니다.

// 1단: 주문 → 배송
public record OrderPaidEvent(
        UUID orderId,
        UUID productId,
        UUID sellerId,
        UUID buyerId,                     // 식별자는 Thin 유지 (추적·정산용)
        String orderType,
        DeliverySnapshot deliverySnapshot // 주소는 Fat (주문 시점 박제)
) {

What Lyft Driver Verification Actually Means

Verification within the Lyft ecosystem refers to the process of confirming that a driver meets the company’s legal, safety, and operational requirements. This process helps ensure that drivers are legitimate individuals who can safely transport passengers.

The verification process usually includes identity confirmation, driver’s license validation, vehicle documentation review, background checks, and in some cases additional regional requirements. Lyft may also request profile photos and insurance documentation to strengthen account authenticity.

A verified driver account also helps reduce fraud within the rideshare ecosystem. Passengers rely heavily on accurate driver profiles, matching photographs, and verified vehicle details before entering a ride. Any compromise in this system could create serious safety concerns.

Why Scammers Target Lyft Driver Accounts

Rideshare driver accounts hold significant value because they are connected to financial information, identity documents, and active earning opportunities. This makes them attractive targets for cybercriminals and scammers.

One common scam involves fake onboarding agencies claiming they can guarantee instant driver approval for a fee. These operators often request sensitive personal information, including Social Security numbers, banking details, and identification documents. Victims may experience identity theft or financial fraud after sharing such data.

Phishing attacks are another major threat. Drivers may receive emails or text messages pretending to come from Lyft support representatives. These messages often contain fake login links designed to steal usernames, passwords, or two-factor authentication codes.

Some scammers also target existing drivers through account takeover schemes. They may call drivers while pretending to be customer support agents and request verification codes or account credentials. Once access is obtained, the scammers can redirect earnings or lock legitimate drivers out of their accounts.

Understanding these risks is the first step toward safely verifying and protecting a Lyft driver account.

Preparing for Safe Lyft Driver Verification

Before starting the verification process, drivers should prepare all required documents and strengthen their digital security practices. Proper preparation helps avoid delays while reducing exposure to fraud.

The first requirement is a valid driver’s license. Drivers should ensure that their license is current, readable, and issued in the region where they intend to operate. Expired or damaged licenses can delay approval significantly.

Vehicle documentation is also essential. Lyft typically requires proof of vehicle registration, insurance coverage, and vehicle inspection depending on local regulations. Drivers should upload only clear, official documents through secure platform channels.

Creating a strong password for the Lyft account is another critical step. Passwords should include a combination of letters, numbers, and symbols while avoiding predictable information such as birthdays or names. Reusing passwords from other websites increases vulnerability to hacking attempts.

Two-factor authentication should be enabled whenever available. This additional security layer helps protect accounts even if passwords become compromised.

Drivers should also verify that they are using the official Lyft application and website before submitting any personal information. Fake apps and cloned websites are common tools used by scammers.

The Official Lyft Driver Verification Process

The official verification process for Lyft drivers is designed to ensure both legal compliance and passenger safety. While procedures may vary slightly depending on location, the general onboarding structure remains similar across most regions.

Applicants typically begin by creating a driver account through the official Lyft platform. They are then asked to provide basic personal information, including legal name, date of birth, and contact details.

Identity verification follows next. Drivers may need to upload a government-issued ID and a profile photo that clearly matches their appearance. This helps passengers identify the correct driver before entering the vehicle.

Background screening is one of the most important stages of the process. Lyft works with third-party screening companies to review criminal records, driving history, and other safety-related factors. This screening process helps maintain passenger trust and regulatory compliance.

Vehicle verification is also required. Lyft reviews submitted vehicle information to confirm that the car meets platform standards regarding age, condition, and insurance requirements.

Drivers should never attempt to bypass or manipulate these official procedures. Providing false documents or misleading information can result in permanent account suspension and possible legal consequences.

Recognizing Fake Lyft Verification Services

Many online scammers target new drivers by advertising fake verification or onboarding assistance services. These schemes often appear convincing because they imitate official branding and customer support language.

One major warning sign is guaranteed approval promises. No legitimate company can guarantee that every applicant will pass background checks or meet eligibility standards. Official verification decisions depend on multiple factors reviewed individually.

Another red flag involves upfront payment requests. Lyft does not require drivers to pay third-party agencies for account verification. Scammers often demand fees through cryptocurrency, gift cards, or peer-to-peer payment apps because these transactions are difficult to reverse.

Suspicious communication methods should also raise concerns. Legitimate support representatives rarely contact drivers through unofficial messaging apps or personal social media accounts. Drivers should communicate only through verified platform channels.

Poorly written emails, unusual URLs, and urgent threats about account suspension are additional indicators of phishing attempts. Scammers often create pressure to encourage impulsive decisions before victims have time to verify authenticity.

Researching official support information and avoiding shortcuts are essential for staying safe during the verification process.

Secure internet connections are equally important. Public Wi-Fi networks may expose transmitted data to interception. Drivers should complete verification steps using trusted private connections whenever possible.

Background checks are a fundamental component of Lyft’s verification system. These screenings help ensure passenger safety while maintaining legal compliance with transportation regulations.

Drivers should also understand local rideshare regulations because requirements may vary significantly between states or cities. Staying compliant with both platform and regional standards helps prevent interruptions in account status.

Avoiding Account Takeover Scams

Account takeover scams have become increasingly common within the rideshare industry. These attacks occur when scammers gain unauthorized access to driver accounts and redirect earnings or lock out legitimate users.

One frequent tactic involves fake support calls. Scammers contact drivers during active rides while pretending to be Lyft support agents investigating a passenger complaint. They then request login credentials or verification codes.

Drivers should remember that legitimate support representatives do not ask for passwords or authentication codes directly. Sharing such information can result in immediate account compromise.

Strong passwords and two-factor authentication significantly reduce takeover risks. Drivers should also avoid using identical credentials across multiple platforms because unrelated data breaches may expose reused passwords.

Phishing emails remain another major threat. Drivers should independently open the official Lyft app rather than clicking suspicious links received through email or text messages.

Immediate action is essential if compromise is suspected. Changing passwords quickly and contacting official support can help limit financial and operational damage.
